Russia's paper in Abu Dhabi, seen by the New York Times, repeats its December 2021 demands, including NATO pulling forces back to 1997 lines and no enlargement. The EU named France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the UK plus the Commission and Council to represent Europe in the talks. The Kremlin has confirmed a Trump–Xi–Putin meeting in Shenzhen on 19 November. Peskov holds his usual weekday briefing on Monday; in December 2025 he called Ukraine's non-accession to NATO 'one of the cornerstones' of talks, while in October 2026 he declined to discuss settlement details publicly.

stories.event: PM Andrej Babiš makes an official visit to Israel from Monday 16 to Wednesday 18 November at the invitation of Benjamin Netanyahu, who remains caretaker prime minister while PM-designate Gadi Eisenkot tries to form a government after the late-October election. Babiš meets Netanyahu on Monday afternoon; on Tuesday he sees President Herzog and Eisenkot and visits Yad Vashem, on Wednesday the Sourasky (Ichilov) Medical Center. He is accompanied by Defence Minister Zůna, Foreign Minister Macinka, Health Minister Vojtěch, Sport and Prevention Minister Šťastný and Chief of the General Staff Hlaváč, who are to meet their Israeli counterparts. Babiš calls anti-ballistic missile defence the main topic: he has met IAI (maker of Arrow, bought by Germany) and Leonardo, and wants to talk to the maker of Barak MX; Czechia's 2021 SPYDER system cannot intercept ballistic missiles. No document to be signed has been announced; in April Macinka and Israel's FM Saar signed an economic-cooperation memorandum and a declaration on a joint commission. The trip replaces Babiš's attendance at 17 November commemorations and is criticised by the opposition and pro-Palestinian groups.

Duffy expects knock-on disruption for a few days and urges Congress to fund the $30.1bn ATC upgrade Trump requested. Monday 16 Nov is the first full business day after the outage; on an ordinary day FlightAware counts roughly 100–250 US cancellations.

stories.event: The Dutch minority cabinet of Prime Minister Rob Jetten (D66, VVD, CDA; 66 of 150 seats) is in crisis after D66 and CDA passed the 2027 tax plan 76–74 on 12 November with the left-wing opposition (PRO, Volt), adding a 38.5% box-3 top rate, against the VVD's votes. After eight hours of talks on Friday, VVD leader and deputy PM Dilan Yeşilgöz called the minority cabinet a 'failed experiment', demanded a 'substantive and political correction' and floated adding a fourth, right-wing party (JA21 is named), which D66 and CDA reject; she said the three might also decide to 'go to the King'. Jetten wants a fresh start and calls a cabinet without the VVD no option. Leaders and group chairs met on Saturday at De Zwaluwenberg under radio silence and resume on Sunday; Jetten cancelled his Monday–Tuesday Caribbean trip, while the King is on Sint Eustatius on Sunday and Monday.

stories.event: Japan's Cabinet Office publishes its first preliminary estimate of July–September 2026 GDP at 08:50 Tokyo time on Monday 16 November (00:50 CET), according to the official ESRI release schedule. A Reuters poll of 16 economists (6 Nov) expects real growth of just 0.1% on the quarter, or 0.3% annualised, down from 1.4% annualised in April–June, which would still be a fourth straight quarter of growth: capital spending is seen up 1.5%, but private consumption is seen falling 0.2% for the first time in seven quarters as the end of energy subsidies raised utility bills, and net exports subtract about 0.4 points on higher crude-oil imports. ITOCHU's research institute expects 1.4% annualised on AI-related investment. Preliminary Japanese GDP regularly misses forecasts by around a point annualised (Q2 2026: 1.1% against 2.0% expected). The figure feeds into the Bank of Japan's December decision, where a rate rise from 1.25% is widely expected.

stories.event: Hungary's new National Asset Recovery and Protection Office (NVVH) said on 13 Nov it had found over HUF 6bn (about $20m) in cash — HUF 5.07bn, €2.66m and $1.26m — buried in forests and hidden in farm buildings, warehouses, a home and a safe during searches on 12–13 Nov in the bribery case against Miklós Seszták, Orbán's development minister in 2014–18 and still a KDNP member of parliament. Seszták, suspected of taking about HUF 12.6bn in kickbacks linked to Volánbusz bus purchases, has been in custody since 28 Sep; on 28 Oct a court extended his detention to 30 January and rejected bail. His lawyer says the money is not his. On Saturday 14 Nov both opposition caucus leaders, KDNP's Bence Rétvári and Fidesz's János Bóka, called on him to give up his seat, and KDNP's Csaba Latorcai initiated a disciplinary procedure and suspension of his party membership. PM Péter Magyar called Fidesz a criminal organisation and urged its MPs to resign. No court hearing or committee session in the case is scheduled for Monday.

stories.event: The Czech Finance Ministry sets maximum retail prices for petrol and diesel in its Cenový věstník each working day under government regulation 203/2026, in force 1–30 November; the price is the average of four three-day wholesale price indices plus a CZK 2.50 margin, with VAT. On Monday 16 November the ministry publishes the next caps; as before the 28 October holiday, they are expected to cover the 17 November holiday and Wednesday 18 November. Diesel futures and the dollar against the crown rose from 11 to 13 November after a fall earlier in the month. The caps and the cut in diesel excise to CZK 8.011 a litre expire on 30 November; Finance Minister Alena Schillerová said on 13 November the government must decide within a week or ten days whether they continue in December.

stories.event: Iran's parliament takes up on Sunday 15 November the double urgency of a plan to drop the 1983 requirement that the intelligence minister hold ijtihad, a senior clerical qualification; every permanent minister since 1984 has been a cleric. The plan would create two bodies inside the ministry, for internal security ('intelligence protection') and ideological affairs, whose heads are appointed directly by Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, while the minister is still nominated by the president and confirmed by parliament. The ministry has had no permanent chief since Esmail Khatib was killed in an Israeli strike in March; President Pezeshkian has nominated no one and the constitutional caretaker limit has long expired. If the double urgency passes, the bill can come to the floor 24 hours after distribution without committee review, and then goes to the Guardian Council.
